'''''Jasminum nudiflorum''''', the '''winter jasmine''', is a slender, [[deciduous]] [[shrub]] [[native plant|native]] to [[China]] ([[Gansu]], [[Shaanxi]], [[Sichuan]], [[Xizang]] ([[Tibet]]), [[Yunnan]]). The flower's blossoming peaks right after winter, which is why it is also named Yingchun ({{lang|zh|迎春}}) in Chinese, which means "the flower that welcomes Spring".  It is widely cultivated as an ornamental and is reportedly naturalized in [[France]] and in scattered locations in the [[United States]] ([[Texas]], [[Oklahoma]], [[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]], [[Tennessee]], [[Maryland]] and [[New Jersey]]).<ref>[https://apps.kew.org/wcsp/namedetail.do?name_id=351463 Kew World Checklist of Selected Plant Families, ''Jasminum nudiflorum'']</ref><ref>[https://bonap.net/MapGallery/County/Jasminum%20nudiflorum.png Biota of North America Program, ''Jasminum nudiflorum'']</ref><ref name="michellekwan">[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=200017786 Flora of China v 15 p 311, ''Jasminum nudiflorum'']</ref>

==Description==
[[File:Jasminum nudiflorum jd plt feuille.jpg|alt=Leaves of Winter Jasmine|thumb|Leaves]]
It grows to {{convert|3|m|ft|0|abbr=on}} tall and wide,<ref name=RHSAZ>{{cite book|title=RHS A-Z encyclopedia of garden plants|year=2008|publisher=Dorling Kindersley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=978-1405332965|pages=1136}}</ref> with arching green shoots and opposite, [[pinnate]], dark green leaves.  Each leaf is divided into three oval-oblong leaflets which are about 3 cm long.<ref name="michellekwan"/><ref>Lindley, John. 1846.  Journal of the Horticultural Society of London 1: 153–154 ''Jasminum nudiflorum''</ref> It is a trailing, vine-like shrub.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Jasminum nudiflorum - Plant Finder|url=https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?kempercode=a152|access-date=2021-12-16|website=www.missouribotanicalgarden.org}}</ref> 

As its name suggests, in the Northern Hemisphere winter jasmine flowers from November to March. The solitary flowers, often appearing on the bare stems (hence the Latin ''nudiflorum'', literally "naked flower")<ref name=RHSLG>{{cite book|last=Harrison|first=Lorraine|title=RHS Latin for gardeners|year=2012|publisher=Mitchell Beazley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=9781845337315|pages=224}}</ref> have six [[petal]]s and are bright yellow, or white, about 1 cm across, appearing in the leaf axils. 

==Taxonomy==
It is known as ''yíng chūn huā'' (迎春花) in Mandarin [[Pinyin]].<ref name=grin/>

It is also known as 'jasmim-amarelo' in [[Portuguese language|Portuguese]] (Brazil) and 'vinterjasmin' in Swedish.<ref name=grin/>

It is called [[Gelsomino d'inverno]] or Gelsomino di San Giuseppe in [[Italiano]].

It was collected in China by [[Robert Fortune]].<ref name=oxford>{{cite book |last1=Nicholson |first1=B.E. |last2=Wallis |first2=Michael |year=1963  |edition=Revised |publication-date=1973 |title=The Oxford Book of Garden Flowers |location=London |publisher=Oxford University Press |page=viii |isbn=1131802403 }}</ref>

It was first published and described by [[John Lindley|Lindl.]] in the Journal of the Horticultural Society of London Vol.1 on page 153 in 1846.<ref name=grin/><ref>{{cite web |title=Oleaceae Jasminum nudiflorum Lindl. |url=https://www.ipni.org/ipni/idPlantNameSearch.do?id=609662-1 |publisher=ipni.org (International Plant Names Index) |access-date=5 August 2015}}</ref>

It was verified by [[United States Department of Agriculture]] and the [[Agricultural Research Service]] on 30 September 2011.<ref name=grin>{{GRIN | accessdate=5 August 2015}}</ref>

==Distribution and range==
It is [[native plant|native]] to China.<ref name=grin/> It is found within many [[Provinces of China]], (including  [[Guangxi]], Gansu,  [[Shanxi]], [[Sichuan]], [[Xizang]] (also referred to as Tibet) and [[Yunnan]].<ref name=grin/>

==Cultivation==
''Jasminum nudiflorum'' is valued by gardeners as one of the few plants that are in flower during the winter months. It is frequently trained against a wall to provide extra warmth and shelter,<ref>{{cite web|title=PFAF Database - ''Jasminum nudiflorum''|url=https://www.pfaf.org/user/Plant.aspx?LatinName=Jasminum+nudiflorum|publisher=Plants for a future|access-date=20 May 2013}}</ref> but also lends itself to [[groundcover]].<ref name=RHSAZ /> It tolerates hard pruning and should be pruned in spring immediately after flowering; regular pruning will help to prevent bare patches. It can also be grown as a [[bonsai]] and is very tolerant of the wiring methods. It likes full sun or partial shade and is hardy.

It has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]]. <ref name = RHSPF>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/9452/Jasminum-nudiflorum/Details | title = ''Jasminum nudiflorum'' | website = www.rhs.org | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | access-date = 25 September 2020}}</ref> 
It can be propagated using the [[layering (horticulture)|layering]] technique.
